papers.title: Study of Laser Shock Peening Impact on the Wettability of Ti-Grade 23 Alloy
papers.abstract: Abstract Titanium and its alloys are extensively used in critical applications due to their exceptional strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. Among these, Ti Grade 23 (Ti-6Al-4V ELI) is particularly valued for its improved ductility, superior fatigue strength, and reduced interstitial elements. This study investigates the effect of Laser Shock Peening (LSP) on the wetting characteristics of Ti Grade 23 alloy, a property essential for enhancing biocompatibility and tribological performance in biomedical and industrial applications. LSP uses a nanosecond laser to impart compressive residual stresses into the alloy’s surface. These stresses lead to surface chemistry, microstructure, and surface energy alterations, collectively influencing wettability. Experiments were conducted by systematically varying two key parameters, the number of laser passes (P) and the water level (L), to explore their combined effect on the alloy’s wettability. The experimental findings reveal a significant transformation in surface wettability, with the contact angle increasing from hydrophilic (65°) to hydrophobic (90°). This transition is attributed to induced compressive stress, surface topography modifications, and crystal structure changes due to the LSP process. The observed wettability alterations suggest that LSP is a viable method for tailoring surface characteristics to meet the requirements of advanced engineering and biomedical applications. This study underscores the potential of LSP as a robust and versatile surface modification technique for Ti Grade 23. The results contribute to the broader understanding of how laser processing parameters influence surface properties, enabling the development of next-generation materials for critical applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V合金的激光冲击强化后处理，但仅研究润湿性，未涉及任何力学性能，因此与用户关注的后处理对疲劳/力学性能的影响不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not examine any mechanical performance metrics (fatigue, tensile strength, hardness) and does not correlate LSP parameters with mechanical properties; it focuses solely on wettability.
